_note: PLAN.md 9. A LIST, not an ID-keyed object, because age ORDER is the meaning
of the data -- keyed by name, the file could be reordered and nothing would
MVP ships age 1 only and never advances (advancement is 9.2), so ages 2-4
carry their numeral and name and nothing else. They are here to fix the
vocabulary and to give the age header (9.1) something to render.
NAMING, decided 2026-08-14 (PLAN.md 9.2.1 item 7): BOTH a numeral and a name.
The numeral is what the HUD shows -- 9.1 is a roman numeral in a gold circle,
which needs no words and fits a 648 px tall canvas. The name is for the places
with room for prose: the tech tree (9.4), the advancement banner, the lobby.
The names are deliberately NOT Age of Empires II's Dark/Feudal/Castle/Imperial
ladder. Those are generic historical terms and carry no legal risk, but this is
an open-source AoE-like and shipping the reference game's exact ladder invites
the comparison for nothing. The fire ladder ties the ages to the game's own
differentiator instead, and lands age 4 on the title.
An earlier version of this file was misaligned by one -- age I was called the
'Feudal Age', which is age 2 in the roster (Age & Unit Planning.md). Fixed
here; the numerals were always right.
_note_advance: advance_time_ticks is how long ADVANCING INTO this age takes, so age 1's is
0 -- every match starts there and nobody advances into it. The sim counts
these ticks (AgeSystem) and the HUD draws them as the ring around the age
badge, so this one number is the whole speed of the age ladder.
100 TICKS IS A TEST VALUE, not a balance one. At SimClock's 10 Hz that is 10
seconds, or 10% of the ring per second -- fast enough to watch all three
advances in one sitting. A real pace is more like 1200 (120 s); the project
owner set the test figure deliberately and it is one number per age to
change back.
ADVANCING NOW COSTS SOMETHING (project owner, 2026-08-27), and the numbers are
Age of Empires II's, which is what they asked for and is a defensible place to
start: 500 food; 800 food + 200 gold; 1000 food + 800 gold. This was the one
field in the file declared and left empty, and the note said so -- a data change
with no code behind it, because AdvanceAgeCommand has always refused a cost the
player could not afford. That prediction held: nothing in the sim changed.
WHAT IT CHANGES IS THE WHOLE SHAPE OF A MATCH, and the AI is where it shows
first. Everybody starts with 200 food, so age 2 is now a real economic goal
reached in minutes rather than a button pressed at t115. The AI's own advance
rules already gate on villager counts, so they wait for the food without any
change -- that is what came of driving them by conditions rather than by ticks.
The names stay ours; only the numbers are borrowed. See the note above on why
the Dark/Feudal/Castle/Imperial ladder is deliberately not used.
`advance_time_ticks` is STILL the 100-tick test value and is a separate decision
from the cost. A real pace is nearer 1200.
